record.paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
record.original_question: When the M-theory action is deformed by higher-order Lovelock and Weyl corrections, are the resulting exact 11-dimensional supergravity cosmological solutions stable, what asymptotic modes do their fields admit, and can this analysis establish a no-hair theorem for an inflationary stage in M-theory?

evidence.quote:
3.5 Stability of 11-dimensional supergravity cosmology I
The aim of this project is to see whether the properties of M-theory cosmologies studied in other projects above are stable with respect to perturbations formed when the M-theory action contains higher order corrections. ... Are these solutions stable? In this problem one expects to trace all possible asymptotic modes of the ﬁelds, and in this way to give the ﬁrst reliable results about the possibility of a no-hair theorem for an inﬂationary stage in M-theory.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider 11-dimensional supergravity, whose bosonic field content consists of a Lorentzian metric $g_{MN}$ on an 11-dimensional manifold and a 3-form gauge potential $A_{MNP}$ with 4-form field strength $F=dA$, governed by the leading-order action
$$S_0=\frac{1}{2\kappa^2}\int d^{11}x\sqrt{-g}\Big(R-\tfrac{1}{2\cdot 4!}F_{MNPQ}F^{MNPQ}\Big)-\frac{1}{12\kappa^2}\int A\wedge F\wedge F.$$
Deform this action by adding higher-curvature corrections of Lovelock type (polynomial scalars built from the Riemann tensor with second-order equations of motion, e.g.\ the Gauss--Bonnet density $\mathcal{L}_{GB}=R^2-4R_{MN}R^{MN}+R_{MNPQ}R^{MNPQ}$ and higher Lovelock densities) together with Weyl-tensor corrections (scalars polynomial in the Weyl tensor $C_{MNPQ}$ such as $C_{MNPQ}C^{MNPQ}$ and contractions of higher powers thereof), giving a corrected action
$$S=S_0+\sum_{k\ge 2}\alpha_k\int d^{11}x\sqrt{-g}\,\mathcal{L}_k(\mathrm{Riem},C),$$
with small coupling constants $\alpha_k$.

Let $(g^{(0)},F^{(0)})$ denote an exact cosmological solution of the corrected equations of motion arising from such an action, with a spatially homogeneous (e.g.\ Bianchi-type or FLRW-like) ansatz on an $(1+10)$-dimensional product or warped geometry, possibly with a portion of the spatial directions compactified.

Address the following:

(a) Determine whether such a cosmological solution is linearly stable under arbitrary smooth perturbations $(\delta g_{MN},\delta A_{MNP})$ of the metric and gauge field, by analyzing the spectrum of the linearized equations of motion derived from $S$.

(b) Classify all asymptotic modes (in cosmic time and in any compactified spatial directions) that the perturbations $(\delta g_{MN},\delta A_{MNP})$ can admit, distinguishing growing, decaying, and oscillatory behaviors.

(c) Using this analysis, decide whether a no-hair theorem holds for an inflationary stage of these corrected 11-dimensional supergravity cosmologies: namely, whether every sufficiently regular perturbation of an inflating background decays (in appropriate norms) so that the late-time geometry approaches the inflationary attractor independently of initial data.
artifact.status_search_result: No definitive resolution was found. The question is posed as an open research project on stability of 11-dimensional supergravity cosmologies under higher-order Lovelock and Weyl corrections, including a possible no-hair theorem for M-theory inflation. While related partial studies exist on higher-curvature corrections to M-theory and on no-hair theorems in higher-dimensional or string cosmology, no source establishes a complete stability analysis or no-hair theorem in this exact setting.
